title: OpenAPI and Swagger UI
summary: Generate API descriptions, inspect Swagger UI, and keep documentation distinct from security enforcement.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: How to Integrate Swagger in Spring Boot | Step-by-Step Tutorial

richText: OpenAPI is a machine-readable description of endpoints, parameters, request bodies, responses and authentication requirements. Swagger UI renders that description as a browser interface.

springdoc-openapi can derive a description from Spring MVC controllers and their Java types. A generated description still needs review: annotations cannot prove that the implementation follows the contract.
Use the UI to inspect a request shape or send a manual request while learning. This is separate from an automated integration test.
For Spring Boot 3, use a compatible springdoc 2.x springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui release. The older Boot 2 course dependency springdoc-openapi-ui belongs to a different compatibility line.
Check the springdoc compatibility matrix against the actual Boot version. Dependency management for Spring starters does not guarantee compatibility for every third-party library.
The usual JSON description is /v3/api-docs. The usual Swagger entry point is /swagger-ui.html, which may redirect to the UI resources.
A schema describes the fields clients can send or receive. Use DTOs so password hashes and persistence-only fields do not accidentally become the documented response.
Document a 201 response and its Location header for resource creation. Document validation and permission failures as well as success.
An OpenAPI security scheme tells API clients how to provide a token. It does not configure Spring Security or authorize a request.
Use deliberate security rules for documentation routes. Public documentation is a product choice; do not make the application’s remaining routes public just to make Swagger work.

springdoc:
  api-docs:
    enabled: true
  swagger-ui:
    enabled: true
Compare the displayed HTTP method, path, request fields and response status with the controller.
Send a valid request, then an invalid one. Confirm that the response follows the documented contract.
If the documentation is outdated, update the annotations or DTOs that own the contract. Editing generated JSON alone will be lost at regeneration.
